steakhouse.name: Aberdeenshire Ribcap
steakhouse.description: 48-day dry-aged on the bone. Cut from Scottish grass-fed Black Angus, the spinalis is the most marbled muscle on the animal. Finished over seasoned oak, served with bone marrow butter and coarse Atlantic salt.

steakhouse.name: Tomahawk for Two
steakhouse.description: A full rib section left attached to the bone, weighing in at over a kilogram. 35-day dry-aged, carved tableside on a walnut board with chimichurri, roasted marrow, and shallot jus.

steakhouse.name: Châteaubriand
steakhouse.description: The quiet end of the tenderloin — no crust to carry it, so the sourcing has to do the talking. Cumbrian suckler beef, cooked sous vide at 52°C then kissed over charcoal. Béarnaise, grilled watercress.

steakhouse.name: Côte de Boeuf
steakhouse.description: Single bone, aged 28 days. Cross-hatched on a screaming hot grate, rested 12 minutes, sliced at the table. The fat cap is the point — render it slowly, don't rush it.

steakhouse.name: Hanger Steak
steakhouse.description: The butcher's cut that rarely makes it to the counter. Coarse-grained, iron-rich, and unreasonably flavourful. Served medium-rare or not at all, with pickled red onion and a sharp Dijon jus.

steakhouse.name: Wagyu Striploin
steakhouse.description: Australian full-blood Wagyu, marble score 8. Less is more: fleur de sel, a sliver of yuzu kosho, and nothing else on the plate that might compete with it.

cafe.name: Ground Espresso
cafe.description: A double shot of our house blend — a 70/30 split of Ethiopian Yirgacheffe and Colombian Huila, roasted in-house every Tuesday. Short, dense, and slightly sweet without sugar.

cafe.name: Flat White
cafe.description: Our most ordered drink and the one we spend the most time calibrating. Ristretto base, whole milk textured to 60°C. The ratio matters here — 1:3, not 1:5.

cafe.name: Filter of the Day
cafe.description: Single-origin, brewed on a Kalita Wave by hand. Origin rotates with what's tasting best — right now: Kenyan Kirinyaga AA, bright with redcurrant and brown sugar. Ask at the counter what's on today.

cafe.name: Kouign-Amann
cafe.description: Baked each morning at 6am. The dough takes three days of lamination and a final hour folded with sugar that caramelises from the outside in. Eat it warm if you can.

cafe.name: Avocado Toast
cafe.description: We weren't going to do it, then we did it properly. Sourdough from the bakery downstairs, smashed avocado with preserved lemon and Aleppo pepper, a soft-poached egg, shaved radish, and a drizzle of our smoked olive oil.

cafe.name: Steak Sandwich
cafe.description: Yesterday's trim from the steakhouse — hanger and flat iron, sliced thin, braised briefly in the jus and loaded into a sourdough roll with caramelised onions, aged cheddar, and horseradish crème.
